questions.question: State Dalton's atomic theory. Write two of its drawbacks.
questions.solution:
**Dalton (1808):** (1) matter consists of indivisible atoms; (2) atoms of an element are identical; (3) compounds form by simple whole-number union of atoms; (4) atoms are indestructible in reactions.

**Drawbacks:** atoms ARE divisible (electrons, protons, neutrons); atoms of an element differ (isotopes); the theory cannot explain bonding or spectra.
questions.knowledgeNote: Dalton explained the laws of chemical combination — the next questions' topic — but isotopes and subatomic particles broke his indivisibility.

questions.question: State the law of multiple proportions and illustrate it with carbon oxides.
questions.solution:
When two elements form more than one compound, the masses of one element combining with a fixed mass of the other are in a small whole-number ratio.

CO: 12 g C joins 16 g O. CO₂: 12 g C joins 32 g O. Oxygen masses 16:32 = **1:2**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Definite proportions (one compound, fixed ratio) vs multiple proportions (several compounds, ratio of ratios) — NEB asks the pair together.

questions.question: State Avogadro's law and write two of its applications.
questions.solution:
**Avogadro's law:** equal volumes of gases at the same T and P contain equal numbers of molecules.

**Applications:** (1) proves diatomic nature of H₂, O₂, N₂ (Gay-Lussac volumes need it); (2) fixes atomic weights via vapour density (M = 2 × VD); (3) 1 mole of any gas occupies 22.4 L at STP.
questions.knowledgeNote: Avogadro reconciled Gay-Lussac's volume ratios with Dalton — H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl needs diatomic molecules.

questions.question: Calculate the number of atoms in 5.6 g of iron. (Fe = 56)
questions.knowledgeNote: Grams → moles (÷ atomic mass) → particles (× Avogadro) is the universal two-step chain.

questions.question: Calculate the percentage of nitrogen in urea, CO(NH₂)₂. (C = 12, O = 16, N = 14, H = 1)
questions.solution:
Molar mass = 12 + 16 + 2(14 + 2) = 60 g/mol. Nitrogen mass = 28 g.

%N = (28/60) × 100 ≈ **46.7%** — the highest N-content of common fertilisers, which is why urea dominates the market.
questions.knowledgeNote: % composition = (total mass of element / molar mass) × 100 — the same step that starts every empirical-formula problem.

questions.question: State Gay-Lussac's law of gaseous volumes with one example.
questions.solution:
When gases react at the same T and P, their volumes are in a small whole-number ratio.

**Example:** 1 vol H₂ + 1 vol Cl₂ → 2 vol HCl (1:1:2).
questions.knowledgeNote: Volume ratios mirror molecule ratios — the law only works for gases, never for solids or liquids.
